item.title: Multiplicativity of Vertex Energy Under the Kronecker Product
item.description: arXiv:2611.33205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that vertex energy is multiplicative under the Kronecker product. Using this core property, we introduce a unified theorem to compute vertex energies for any graph operation obtained through the Kronecker product. As direct applications, we derive exact vertex energy formulas for semishadow, generalized splitting, and shadow-splitting graphs. Furthermore, we completely classify all blueprint matrices that preserve vertex energies.
item.dc:creator: Ronak B Dudhat, Vinodray J Kaneria, Kalpesh M Popat

item.title: Constructions and Upper Bounds for Trifferent Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.33212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A ternary code of blocklength $n$ is trifferent if every three distinct codewords have a coordinate at which they take all three values. Let $T(n)$ be the largest size of such a code. We prove that $T(n)=\Omega(1.162579^n)$ and $T(n)=O(n^{-1/2}(3/2)^n)$. The lower bound improves the exponential base $(9/5)^{1/4}=1.15829\ldots$ of K\"orner and Marton. It comes from a random system of overlapping local constraints, in which every position is read two or three times, followed by thinning and the deletion of nearby pairs and of the remaining triples that violate trifference. The required estimates reduce to finitely many inequalities, which we verify rigorously by computer. The upper bound improves our earlier bound $O(n^{-2/5}(3/2)^n)$.
item.dc:creator: Siddharth Bhandari, Abhishek Khetan

item.title: Graphs with the largest chainable index and their properties
item.description: arXiv:2611.33355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper provides a complete characterization of the set of graphs with the largest chainable index. In particular, it is shown that the number of arcs and vertex degrees of such graphs satisfy strong restrictions. Moreover, graphs with the largest chainable index form five parametric families, and exactly one of them consists of graphs that are not strongly connected. As a consequence, the number of graphs on $n$ vertices with the largest chainable index is computed, and the values of the primitive exponent for these graphs are calculated.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Guterman, Svetlana Zhilina, Evgenii Shafeev

item.title: Nash-Williams' Orientation Theorems for Infinite Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.33366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nash-Williams proved in 1960 that every finite multigraph has a \emph{well-balanced} orientation: for all vertices $x$ and $y$, the maximum number of arc-disjoint directed paths from $x$ to $y$ is at least half, rounded down, of the maximum number of edge-disjoint $x$--$y$ paths. In particular every finite $2k$-edge-connected multigraph has a $k$-arc-connected orientation. He announced an extension to infinite graphs whose details, as far as is known, never appeared, and the two statements for infinite graphs have since been known as the strong and the weak orientation conjecture of Nash-Williams. We prove both, for multigraphs of arbitrary cardinality. For multigraphs with countably many edges we obtain more: a well-balanced orientation that is smooth (in-degree and out-degree differ by at most one at every vertex of finite degree) and, if the multigraph is $2$-edge-connected, has infinitely many arcs in each direction across every infinite cut. Such an orientation is obtained by K\H{o}nig's lemma from a sequence of finite orientation problems, each solved by the theorem of Kir\'aly and Szigeti on simultaneous well-balanced orientations. The infinite cuts are controlled by a canonical tree of $2$-edge-connected pieces with finite cores: once the cores are strongly connected and every finite cut is crossed in both directions, every arc lies on a directed cycle that uses only edges owned by one piece and edges of the cores of its children, and a counting argument of Thomassen does the rest. Neither local finiteness nor ends play any role.
item.dc:creator: Amena Assem, Mohammad A. Mahmoud, Bobby Miraftab

item.title: Graceful Colorings for Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.33427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a vertex coloring $c:V(G)\to [k]$, the graceful induced edge labeling is the induced edge coloring $c'(uv):=|c(u)-c(v)|$. A vertex coloring $c$ is a \textbf{graceful coloring} if $c$ is a proper vertex coloring and $c'$ is a proper edge coloring. The graceful coloring number $\chi_g(G)$ is the least $k$ such that there exists a graceful coloring $c:V(G)\to [k]$. We study the graceful coloring number for the Erd\H{o}s-Renyi random graph, $G_{n,p}$. In the diameter $2$ regime, we find the $\chi_g(G_{n,p})=n^{1+o(1)}$ using a connection between graceful colorings and Salem-Spenser sets. In the regime where $G_{n,p}$ is connected, but not diameter 2, we find that $\chi_g(G_{n,p})=\Theta\left(\frac{n^2p^2}{\log np}\right)$, using the forbidden submatching method and a connection between graceful coloring and the chromatic number of the square of $G_{n,p}$. Finally, in the regime where $G_{n,p}$ has constant average degree, we find that $\chi_g(G_{n,p})=\Delta(G_{n,p})+1$, by exploring the cycle structure of $G_{n,p}$.
item.dc:creator: Sean English, Edward Janosko, Erik Slivken, Sid Touzeau

item.title: Inverses of split graphs via Ferrers diagrams and degree sequences
item.description: arXiv:2611.33535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph is a split graph if its vertex set can be partitioned into a clique and a stable set and is a partitioned split graph if the partition is also specified. The inverse of a partitioned split graph is formed by removing all edges within the clique and adding all edges between vertices in the stable set, while preserving the edges between the two parts. In this paper we compare two forms of the degree sequence of a graph: the conventional form and the block representation. We show the effect on the block representation of taking complements of graphs and inverses of split graphs, the latter of which is complicated by the fact that some split graphs have two different inverses. When there are two distinct inverses, we show how the degree sequences of these inverses are related to each other in both the conventional and block representations. We also demonstrate geometric interpretations of these results using Ferrers diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Karen L. Collins, Tantan Dai, Ann N. Trenk

item.title: Graphon hitting times: connectivity and minimum degree
item.description: arXiv:2611.33540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A classical result in random graphs states that the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph process becomes connected at exactly the moment its last isolated vertex disappears. The main goal of this paper is to establish a graphon analogue of this result. Let $G(n,W)$ be the inhomogeneous random graph sampled from a graphon $W$, and reveal its edges one by one in a uniformly random order. We prove that if $W$ is connected and the lower tail of its degree distribution satisfies $g_W(t)/t\to 0$ as $t\to 0$, which is needed for the connectivity of $G(n,W)$, then the connectivity and minimum-degree-one hitting times coincide asymptotically almost surely. We also determine when this hitting time occurs at scale $\Theta(n\log n)$, as in the binomial random graph model. Moreover, we give a simple analytic criterion for the transition to be localized in a $(1+o(1))$-multiplicative window, and construct graphons with minimum degrees arbitrarily close to zero whose transition is nevertheless sharp. Our approach uses Laplace transforms and vague convergence of rescaled graphon degree measures to provide a unified framework for analyzing low-degree vertices and connectivity transitions. Along the way, we revisit the minimum degree of~$G(n,W)$, giving simplified proofs of results of Hladk\'y and Viswanathan~\cite{HV} and establishing the limiting distribution of $\delta(G(n,W))$ under a second-order decorrelation condition.
item.dc:creator: Constanza Gacit\'ua Fuentes, Marcos Kiwi, Mat\'ias Pavez-Sign\'e

item.title: Helly complexes are minimal fillings
item.description: arXiv:2611.33548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that Helly complexes are universal minimal fillings. More precisely, if $X$ is a Helly complex, and $Y$ is a simplicial complex whose boundary is isomorphic to that of $X$ and such that the distances between the boundary vertices induced by $Y$ are at least as large as those induced by $X$, then $Y$ has at least as many vertices as $X$. The same type of inequalities hold for $i$-dimensional simplices of $X$ and $Y$ for all $i=0,1,\ldots$, i.e., for all coordinates of the $f$-vectors of $X$ and $Y$. When $Y$ is dismantlable, we show that the boundary isomorphism assumption can be weakened to a bijection between the vertex sets of both boundaries with an additional technical condition on boundary edges.
item.dc:creator: Mart\'in Blufstein, J\'er\'emie Chalopin, Victor Chepoi

item.title: Reflection subgroups and the Lookup Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.33572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Lookup Conjecture of Boe-Graham proposes a Bruhat graph criterion for rational smoothness of Schubert varieties in the flag variety $\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{B}$ of a complex reductive group. Its extension to Kac-Moody groups of affine type $\widetilde{A}_n$ was considered by Graham-Li. We prove the original conjecture as well as its extension to $\widetilde{A}_n$. Our method could be applied more generally to any Kac-Moody group after checking the rank-three reflection subgroups of its Weyl group. We also prove a parabolic version of the Lookup Conjecture for the type $A$ affine Grassmannian, where a stronger Bruhat graph degree monotonicity property in fact holds, and discuss the implication via the geometric Satake correspondence for weight multiplicities.
item.dc:creator: Christian Gaetz, Yibo Gao

item.title: Reflections in graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.33575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study an operation on graphs, called edge reflection, modeled on the effect of a reflection on the inversion graph of a permutation. The edge reflection length of a graph counts the fewest edge reflections needed to reduce it to the edgeless graph. Emptying a graph one edge at a time, or one vertex at a time, gives two upper bounds on this length, and each holds with equality precisely when the graph is a forest. For the edge bound we say more: the cyclomatic number of the graph bounds, above and below, the difference between the graph's size and its edge reflection length. Returning to permutations, we show that the edge reflection length of an inversion graph is at most the reflection length of any permutation realizing it, with equality whenever each connected component of the inversion graph has cyclomatic number at most one.
item.dc:creator: Sean Mandrick, Bridget Eileen Tenner, Vincent Vatter

item.title: Generalized oriented chromatic numbers and directed generalized coloring numbers of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.33681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $q$, we bound the $q$-transitive oriented chromatic number $\chi_o^q(G)$ in terms of the directed weak coloring number $\overrightarrow{wcol}_{2q}(G)$. For orientations with no directed cycle of length at most $2q$, we compare $q$-transitive oriented colorings with $\vec P_{2q}$-preserving oriented colorings. We also show that the directed strong coloring number at radius $2k-1$ bounds the density of every depth-$(k-1)$ shallow topological minor of $G$. These results characterize bounded expansion in terms of directed coloring numbers, oriented colorings, and homomorphisms of acyclic orientations.
item.dc:creator: Wenwen Li, Jaroslav Nesetril, Daqing Yang

item.title: The maximum number of triangles in a graph without pentagons
item.description: arXiv:2611.33685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The generalized Tur\'an number $\ex(n,T,H)$ is the maximum number of $T$ in an $n$-vertex graph containing no $H$. Inspired by a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s on the function $\ex(n,C_5,K_3)$, Bollob\'as and Gy\H ori proposed the problem of $\ex(n,K_3,C_5)$. In this paper, we prove that $\ex(n,K_3,C_5)=(1/(3\sqrt3)+o(1))n^{3/2}$, finally solved this problem. As applications, we determine the asymptotic value of $\ex(n,\{\text{ind-}C_4,C_{5}\})$ which answers a question of Ergemlidze, Gy\H{o}ri and Methuku, and the asymptotic value of 3-uniform hypergraph without Berge short cycle which solve a conjecture of Gy\H{o}ri and Salia.
item.dc:creator: Qing Cui, Ervin Gy\H{o}ri, Chenke Zhang, Xiutao Zhu

item.title: Topological Clique Exclusion in Positively Curved Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.33694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study locally finite graphs of positive Lin--Lu--Yau curvature and minimum degree at least $t-1$ under two exclusions: a topological $K_t$, denoted $TK_t$, and its locally topological version $TK^{(\leq2)}_t$, in which every replacement path has length at most two. The ordinary exclusion gives an $O(t^{7})$ maximum-degree bound by combining the classical density theorem for topological cliques with a curvature-driven rainbow-clique argument. For $K_t$-minor-free graphs, a Hall-matching refinement improves the maximum-degree bound to $O(t^3(\log t)^{3/2})$ and, for connected graphs, the order bound to $O(t^{19}(\log t)^9)$. For the weaker local exclusion, a codegree graph and Ramsey's theorem give the bound $\exp(O(t\log t))$. We also prove an exponential maximum-degree bound when the full 1-subdivision $K_t^{(2)}$ is forbidden as a subgraph, assuming minimum degree at least $t$.
item.dc:creator: Linyuan Lu

item.title: Low treebandwidth colorings, $p$-centred colorings and generalized coloring numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.33701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $p$, let $\chi^{tb}_p(G)$ be the minimum number of colors in a vertex coloring such that every subgraph induced by $i$ color classes has treebandwidth at most $i-1$, for $1\le i\le p$. We establish quantitative relationships between these coloring parameters and generalized coloring numbers. If $\operatorname{wcol}_{2p}(G)\le m$, then $G$ admits a $p$-centred coloring with at most $[(p+1)m]^m$ colors; in particular, $\chi^{tb}_p(G)\le[(p+1)m]^m$. Conversely, if $\chi^{tb}_{k+1}(G)\le m$, then $\col_k(G) \le 1+4k^4\binom{m}{k+1}^{2}.$ Consequently, a graph class has bounded expansion if and only if its low treebandwidth coloring numbers are uniformly bounded for every fixed parameter. This gives a characterization of bounded expansion in terms of colorings defined by bounded ancestor distances in rooted forest layouts.
item.dc:creator: Wenwen Li, Daqing Yang

item.title: A degree-stability method for the $p$-spectral Tur\'an-type problem for disjoint color-critical graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.33921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F_1,\ldots,F_t$ be pairwise vertex-disjoint color-critical graphs with $\chi(F_i)=r+1$ for each $i\in[t]$. For $r\ge 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, Simonovits [Discrete Math. 7 (1974) 349--376] proved that the graph $K_{t-1}\vee T_{n-t+1,r}$ uniquely maximizes the number of edges among $n$-vertex graphs containing no copy of $\cup_{i=1}^tF_i$. In 2024, Lei and Li [Electron. J. Combin. 31 (2024), P1.25] established the corresponding result for the adjacency spectral radius. We prove that, for every fixed $p>1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, the same graph uniquely maximizes the $p$-spectral radius in this class. The proof reduces the problem to forbidding $t$ disjoint copies of a single color-critical graph and applies degree stability after deleting $t-1$ such copies.
item.dc:creator: Jian Zheng, Ya-Lei Jin, Ming-Zhu Chen, Peng-Li Zhang

item.title: On a Problem of Erd\H{o}s and Graham Related to Restricted Order
item.description: arXiv:2611.33191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A$ be a set of nonnegative integers. We prove that if $A\setminus F$ has a finite order for every finite subset $F\subseteq A$, then $A$ has finite restricted order. This resolves a problem posed by Erd\H{o}s and Graham in 1980. We also establish a local to global principle to characterize restricted asymptotic bases of finite order.
item.dc:creator: Shi-Qiang Chen, Quan-Hui Yang, Lilu Zhao

item.title: Semisimple-Unipotent Decomposition and the Exact Order of a Linear Cellular Automaton over F_2
item.description: arXiv:2611.33216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the linear cellular automaton on the cyclic graph $C_n$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ defined by the local rule $v_i(t+1)=v_{i-1}(t)\oplus v_i(t)\oplus v_{i+1}(t)$ (Wolfram's Rule 150 under periodic boundary conditions). Identifying the configuration space $V_n=\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $R_n = \mathbb{F}_2[x] / \langle x^n - 1 \rangle$, the evolution operator corresponds to multiplication by $G(x)=1+x+x^{n-1}$. We re-derive the invertibility criterion $3\nmid n$, classify periodic and transient behaviour, and prove that Hamming weight is non-monotone for every $n\ge3$. We then factor $x^n-1$ via the Chinese Remainder Theorem and separate semisimple contributions governed by finite-field multiplicative orders from unipotent contributions governed by Frobenius squaring. We determine the exact local unipotent orders and obtain a closed-form global order $r(A)$: $r(A)=2^{m-1}$ for $n=2^m$ with $m\ge2$, while for $n=2^m q$, $q>1$ odd and $3\nmid n$, $r(A)=2^m\operatorname{lcm}(m_2,\ldots,m_r)$. The theory is illustrated by $n=5,7,8,16$ and computationally verified for small dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Ana Boji\'c

item.title: The smallest vertex triangle in a fixed polygon
item.description: arXiv:2611.33233v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Among the triangles determined by $n$ points in convex position in the unit square, one has area at most $32/n^3$. Equality is possible exactly when $4$ divides $n$, and then the maximizing point set is unique. We prove a fixed-container theorem for a class of convex $s$-gons that includes affinely regular polygons and a one-parameter family of pairwise affinely inequivalent hexagons without a centre of symmetry. If the container has equal ears of area $a$ and the tips of its directed side vectors are in convex position, the sharp bound at $n=sk$ is $a/k^3$. Its equality conditions determine every side vector of the maximizing polygon. The proof uses the area enclosed by the normalized side directions. We compare the result with the area-normalized smallest-ear theorem of Gronchi and Longinetti and give consequences for unrestricted Heilbronn configurations with 13 and 15 points.
item.dc:creator: Dawid Trela

item.title: The regular polygon maximizes the first positive Steklov eigenvalue among simple polygons at fixed area
item.description: arXiv:2611.33253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $N\ge5$ and every simple planar polygon $P$ with at most $N$ sides, $\sqrt{|P|}\,\sigma_1(P)\le\sqrt{|R_N|}\,\sigma_1(R_N)$, where $\sigma_1$ is the first positive Steklov eigenvalue and $R_N$ is a regular $N$-gon. Equality holds precisely for polygons similar to $R_N$. This answers Oudet's fixed-area open problem \cite{AIM} for all $N\ge5$.
item.dc:creator: Senping Luo, Bingbing Xie

item.title: From random intersection to spatial graphs: a unified asymptotic framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.33423v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Random intersection graphs and spatial random graphs provide different mechanisms for generating edges and clustering. We investigate their interplay through geometric random intersection graphs, where vertices are adjacent whenever they share a spatially located group. First, a Poisson decomposition by attachment sets yields exact subgraph probabilities and laws of large numbers for connected subgraph densities. It distinguishes triangles supported by a common group from those requiring three distinct groups. Second, explicit representations of global and average local clustering reveal their different dependence on model parameters and the role of shared groups in edge correlations. Finally, by varying the strength and spatial range of group memberships, we establish convergence to random connection, random geometric, random intersection, Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi, and complete graphs. We characterize the corresponding clustering limits and show that clustering need not converge to that of the limiting graph, highlighting the distinction between spatially local convergence and global graph statistics.
item.dc:creator: Alessandra Bianchi, Alberto De Nicol\`o, Riccardo Michielan

item.title: Fast Algorithms for Permanents of Permutationally-Dominant Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.33485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a fast algorithm for approximating the permanent of permutationally-dominant matrices. In particular, we obtain a fully polynomial randomised approximation scheme whose runtime is quadratic in both the dimension of the matrix and the inverse of the approximation error. Our approach is based on a polymer model representation of the permanent and importance sampling of the logarithm of its partition function via the theory of heaps of pieces of Viennot.
item.dc:creator: Ryan L. Mann

item.title: On the Cluster Duration Distribution of the Markovian Hawkes Process
item.description: arXiv:2611.33494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The duration of a Hawkes process cluster, meaning the time from first point to last point in an entirely endogenously generated progeny stream, has been stubbornly resistant to analysis; even the mean has not been known in closed form. Recently, uniformly random parking functions have been found to be hidden spines of these history-driven clusters, offering a probabilistic combinatorial structure within self-excitement that has opened new avenues for analysis. Here, we leverage and refine this decomposition to provide a closed-form expression for the mean cluster duration in the case of an exponential excitation kernel. Specifically, we reduce from uniformly random parking functions to non-uniform preference counts. This change of probabilistic combinatorial structure in the decomposition leads us to both a Borel-based identity and an explicit integral-based expression for the mean duration.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Daw, Amer Goel

item.title: A proof of the Nevo-Peeva conjecture: Exact regularity and linear powers of gap-free edge ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.33501v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with at least one edge, and let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal over a field $K$. We prove that if $G$ is gap-free, then $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q=\max\{2q,\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)+q-1\}$ for all $q\geq 1$. This answers both open problems of Nevo and Peeva on ordinary powers: $I(G)^q$ has a linear resolution exactly when $q\geq \mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, and their proposed regularity recurrence holds with equality. As consequences, the upper bound $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q\leq 2q+\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-2$ conjectured by Alilooee, Banerjee, Beyarslan, H\`a, Jayanthan and Selvaraja holds for gap-free graphs; every power $I(G)^q$ with $q\geq 2$ has a linear resolution when $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)=3$; and the stabilization index equals $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, which is unbounded on this class. The proof rests on a combinatorial result of independent interest: a parity-sensitive homology vanishing theorem for a filtration of the independence complex by a weighted Hall defect. An internalization lemma and sublevel complexes of submodular functions control the local terms, and Hall's theorem together with an implication-digraph argument classifies the zero level. A capacitated form of the Tutte-Berge formula and Takayama's formula identify the filtration with the degree complexes of ordinary powers. The algebraic statements hold over every field, and the topological vanishing holds with arbitrary abelian coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Luis Alfredo Dupont Garc\'ia

item.title: Extension complexity is not additive under Cartesian products
item.description: arXiv:2611.33631v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the linear extension complexity of a Cartesian product of polytopes can be strictly smaller than the sum of the extension complexities of its factors. This disproves Conjecture 1.2 of Grande, Padrol and Sanyal. We construct a rational 24-dimensional polytope $P$ with 50 facets and 150 vertices such that $P$ has extension complexity 40 and $P \times P$ has extension complexity exactly 79. We also prove that the saving can be arbitrarily large, even in a Cartesian square: for every $t$ there is a rational polytope $R_t$ whose square needs at least $t$ fewer inequalities than two separate copies of $R_t$. For two different factors, we construct a family whose product saves at least $\lceil 5n/27 \rceil$ inequalities while the two separate complexities sum to $O(n)$, so that the saving is a constant fraction of the total. The proofs rest on a transfer theorem: wedging over the omitted facets of a polytope turns a gap between the nonnegative ranks of partial slack matrices into a gap between extension complexities. The unbounded squares come from intersecting families of sets on successively larger alphabets. In the square the two copies of each coordinate share generators, while a counting lemma determines the exact cost of a single factor.
item.dc:creator: Minhao Liu

item.title: Explicit covers and rigid obstructions for simplicial complexity: from spheres to surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.33804v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The strict simplicial complexity $SC_{\rm strict}(K)$, Gonz\'alez's simplicial complexity at subdivision level zero, is one less than the least number of contiguity domains covering the ordered product $K\times K$. We bound it from both sides. For upper bounds, every product of two vertex stars is a domain, which gives $SC_{\rm strict}(K)\le\rho(K)-1$ for an exactly computable set-cover number $\rho(K)$; the bound is sharp on every even-dimensional simplex boundary. A GPU annealer that evolves whole systems of contiguity chains finds three-domain covers of $\partial\Delta^3,\dots,\partial\Delta^7$ and of the cube boundary. Seeded by star covers, it descends from $24$ to $5$ domains on the icosahedron boundary, and an exact SAT completion of its stalled state gives $SC_{\rm strict}\le3$ there. For lower bounds, a subcomplex of $K\times K$ is rigid if its two projections are joined by no contiguity chain of any length; $k$ domains can cover $K\times K$ only if $k$ classes of facets avoid every rigid subcomplex, a finite SAT problem. Rigid subcomplexes arise from hollow triangles over essential empty triangles and, on complexes without dominated vertices, from the graph of every order-preserving simplicial self-map other than the identity. The resultingchain-length-free bounds give $SC_{\rm strict}(\partial\Delta^{n+1})=2>1=TC(S^n)$ for $n=3,5,7,9$, $SC_{\rm strict}=2>1$ for the five-vertex M\"obius band, $SC_{\rm strict}\ge3>2$ for the seven-vertex torus, and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le5$ and $4\le SC_{\rm strict}\le6$ for two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$. They also sort the annealer's stalls: on these two triangulations of $\mathbb{RP}^2$, the Klein bottle and $\partial\Delta^4$, almost every uncovered facet closes a rigid subcomplex in every domain, while the icosahedron stall was a search failure.
item.dc:creator: M. Perez, J. Flores

item.title: PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.33966v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: There are several approaches to AI-driven mathematical discovery. One of these involves the use of large language models (LLMs) to resolve well-specified conjectures via text-based reasoning, while another uses narrow models and interpretability for more open-ended, human-in-the-loop exploration using object-based mathematical data. The latter is limited in its ability to move beyond simple empirical pattern detection while the former is not well-designed for direct, open-ended exploration of large mathematical datasets. In this paper we introduce PatternMiner, a system that combines these two paradigms. In PatternMiner, an LLM agent generates mathematical datasets based on an initial broad question, trains narrow machine learning models on them, uses interpretability techniques to extract patterns from these trained models, and uses these patterns to formulate conjectures. Once an initial conjecture has been formulated, PatternMiner instructs the agent to search for counterexamples using calls to mathematical software. If a set of counterexamples can be found, these are used as feedback for conjecture refinement or another round of training and interpretability. The conjecture progressively evolves through this iterative sequence with the agent allowed to try to prove it at any point. We describe the results of applying PatternMiner to five well-known positivity problems in algebraic combinatorics. PatternMiner proves several new theorems related to Schubert positivity and projection, a character-row evaluation formula, a restricted version of the Kazhdan--Lusztig combinatorial invariance conjecture, and Schur positivity for a family of immanant coefficients. We end by analyzing the most common routes to conjecture generation that are used by PatternMiner in our case studies as well as documenting the most common failure modes.
item.dc:creator: Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, Emily Xia Meng, Henry Kvinge

item.title: Playing through a noisy channel (and knowing it)
item.description: arXiv:2012.06768v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study combinatorial games played through a noisy channel, where the move chosen by a player may differ from the move that is effectively executed. The key feature of this setting is that any received legal move is accepted as the move played, regardless of the player's original intention, while illegal moves trigger retransmission. Both players know the error mechanism and strategically choose their transmitted moves to maximize their winning probabilities. This interaction between strategic choice and imperfect execution gives rise to a rich class of games whose behavior can differ substantially from that of the underlying combinatorial game. We develop a general framework based on move error functions and establish structural results concerning winning probabilities, optimal moves, and conditions for fair chance games. We then investigate in detail one-pile Nim with independent binary transmission errors. Despite its apparent simplicity, this example exhibits unexpectedly intricate behavior. We determine optimal strategies and winning probabilities in the low-error regime and uncover a substantially richer structure in the high-error regime, including changes in optimal play and nontrivial limiting behavior.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Capitelli, Melina Privitelli

item.title: A very short proof of Sidorenko's inequality for counts of homomorphism between graphs
item.description: arXiv:2408.01478v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A fundamental extremality result due to Sidorenko (Discrete Math. 131.1-3, 1994) states that among all connected graphs G on k vertices, the k-vertex star maximises the number of graph homomorphisms of G into any graph H. We provide a new short proof of this result using only a simple recursive counting argument for trees and H\"older's inequality.
item.dc:creator: Lukas L\"uchtrath, Christian M\"onch

item.title: Infinite families of planar graphs of a given injective chromatic number
item.description: arXiv:2412.09969v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An injective colouring of a graph is a colouring in which every two vertices sharing a common neighbour receive a different colour. Chen, Hahn, Raspaud and Wang conjectured that every planar graph of maximum degree $\Delta \ge 3$ admits an injective colouring with at most $\lceil 3\Delta/2\rceil$ colours. This was later disproved by Lu\v{z}ar and \v{S}krekovski for certain small and even values of $\Delta$ and they proposed a new refined conjecture. Using an algorithm for determining the injective chromatic number of a graph, i.e. the smallest number of colours for which the graph admits an injective colouring, we give computational evidence for Lu\v{z}ar and \v{S}krekovski's conjecture and extend their results by presenting an infinite family of $3$-connected planar graphs for each $\Delta$ (except for $4$) attaining their bound, whereas they only gave a finite amount of examples for each $\Delta$. Hence, together with another infinite family of maximum degree $4$, we provide infinitely many counterexamples to the conjecture by Chen et al. for each $\Delta$ if $4\le \Delta \le 7$ and every even $\Delta \ge 8$. We provide similar evidence for analogous conjectures by La and \v{S}torgel and Lu\v{z}ar, \v{S}krekovski and Tancer when the girth is restricted as well. Also in these cases we provide infinite families of $3$-connected planar graphs attaining the bounds of these conjectures for certain maximum degrees $\Delta\geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Matias Daneels, Jan Goedgebeur, Jarne Renders

item.title: On fractional triangle decompositions of random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.15877v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that with high probability $G(n,p)$ with $p \geq n^{-4/11 + o(1)}$ admits a fractional triangle decomposition (FTD), i.e., a nonnegative weighting of its triangles such that for each edge, the total weight of the triangles containing it equals one. This improves on the state of the art, due to Delcourt, Kelly, and Postle, that $p \geq n^{-1/3+o(1)}$ suffices. The proof is algorithmic: Given $G \sim G(n,p)$, we first construct an approximate FTD by taking a uniform weighting of the triangles. We then use specialized gadgets to iteratively shift weights and obtain successively better approximations of an FTD.
item.dc:creator: Ghaura Mahabaduge, Michael Simkin

item.title: The $d$-gonal locus in the moduli space of tropical plane curves
item.description: arXiv:2511.20805v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce and study the locus $\mathbb{M}_{g,d}^\textrm{nd}$ of genus $g$ tropical plane curves of gonality $d$ inside the moduli space $\mathbb{M}^{\textrm{nd}}_{g}$ of tropical plane curves of genus $g$. Each such tropical curve arises from a Newton polygon, and we conjecture that the gonality of the tropical curve is equal to an easily computed parameter of this polygon called the expected gonality, closely related to the lattice width of the polygon. Let $\mathbb{M}_{g,{\underline{d}}}^\textrm{nd}$ denote the locus of tropical curves whose associated Newton polygon has expected gonality $d$. We prove that for fixed $d$ and sufficiently large genus $g$, the dimensions of these two loci agree: \[ \\dim\left(\mathbb{M}_{g,d}^\textrm{nd}\right) =\dim\left(\mathbb{M}_{g,{\underline{d}}}^\textrm{nd}\right). \] Our results provide evidence that, in sufficiently high genus compared to expected gonality, the gonality of a tropical curve is determined by the expected gonality of the Newton polygon from which it arises. We also leverage our results to prove bounds on the dimensions of moduli spaces of non-degenerate algebraic curves.
item.dc:creator: Desmond Leitz, Ralph Morrison, S{\o}ren Newman-Taylor, Vincent X. Wang

item.title: An asymptotically tight upper bound for the domination number of the $2$-token graph of path graphs
item.description: arXiv:2601.20216v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note, we show that the domination number of the $2$-token graph of the path graph of order $n\geq 2$ is equal to $\frac{n^2}{10}+\Theta(n)$.
item.dc:creator: E. Acosta Troncoso, J. Lea\~nos, L. M. Rivera

item.title: An assortment of problems in permutation patterns: unimodality, equivalence, derangements, and sorting
item.description: arXiv:2602.16355v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We collect open problems in permutation patterns on four themes: rank-unimodality in the permutation pattern poset and log-convexity of principal classes, Wilf-equivalence and shape-Wilf-equivalence, the enumeration of derangements in permutation classes, and sorting by stacks in series, generalized stacks, and restricted containers (C-machines).
item.dc:creator: Vincent Vatter

item.title: Certified Return-Word Induction for a Perturbed Hofstadter Recursion: Global well-definedness, local frequencies and nonautomaticity
item.description: arXiv:2603.29622v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the parity-perturbed Hofstadter recursion $Q(1)=Q(2)=1$, $Q(n)=Q(n-Q(n-1))+Q(n-Q(n-2))+(-1)^n$. We give a computer-assisted proof of global well-definedness using 13 return words, 92 synchronized states and 122 two-source rules. An induction on the rank words identifies the four ordered physical source projections at every level. The marked word construction and a finite lag certificate then identify its binary output with the step word $s_j=(Q(j+1)-Q(j-1))/2$ of the recursion. We determine the frequency of $001100$ in prefixes of $s$ as a function of the position within each pair of epochs. After rescaling the prefix length by $4^m/3$, the frequency converges uniformly to an explicit profile. Its minimum $1/96$ and maximum $1/48$ are the exact lower and upper limiting frequencies, and every value between them is a subsequential limit. The longest alternating factor among the first $N$ steps has length $2\log_2 N+O(1)$. It follows from Cobham's gap theorem that neither the step word nor $Q\bmod 4$ is automatic in any integer base $k\ge 2$.
item.dc:creator: Marco Mantovanelli

item.title: Inherited conics in Andr\'e planes of odd order
item.description: arXiv:2606.11763v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The process of deriving the Desarguesian plane $PG(2,q^2)$ to get the Hall plane is well known, and the problem of when a conic in $PG(2,q^2)$ inherits to an arc in the Hall plane has been solved. In this article we look at the generalisation of replacing an Andr\'e net of $PG(2,q^t)$, $t\geq 3$ to construct an Andr\'e plane of order $q^t$. This article looks at the case where $q$ is odd and $t$ is prime, and determines when a conic in $PG(2,q^t)$ inherits to an arc in an Andr\'e plane. We first consider replacing a single Andr\'e net, then generalise to replacing multiple Andr\'e nets, and obtain results in Andr\'e and subregular planes. Further, the number of arcs that are inherited from a single Andr\'e replacement is determined.
item.dc:creator: S. G. Barwick, Alice M. W. Hui, Wen-Ai Jackson

item.title: Vertex-transitive strongly regular graphs in the switching class of doubly transitive two-graphs
item.description: arXiv:2608.30330v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a finite two-graph whose full automorphism group $G$ is $2$-transitive. Up to complementation, we classify the primitive strongly regular graphs with associated two-graph $\mathcal{T}$ whose full automorphism group is a transitive maximal subgroup of $G$ and does not contain the largest perfect subgroup of $G$. In doing so, we obtain a new family of vertex-transitive strongly regular graphs whose associated two-graph arises from $P\Sigma L(2,q)$.
item.dc:creator: Robert F. Bailey, G\'abor P. Nagy, Valentino Smaldore

item.title: Ramsey-type results for Maker-Breaker games
item.description: arXiv:2609.02588v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph $G$ is minimal Ramsey for a graph $H$ if every $2$-colouring of the edges of $G$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$, but for every proper subgraph of $G$, there is a $2$-colouring that does not contain such a monochromatic copy. Characterizing minimal Ramsey graphs is a widely studied problem. Recent research in this field includes the characterization of the size of the set $\mathcal{M}_2(H)$ of all minimal Ramsey graphs for $H$, or finding the smallest minimum degree among all graphs in $\mathcal{M}_2(H)$. In this paper, we introduce a game theoretic analogue of the above concept by considering the Maker-Breaker $H$-game on a graph $G$. In this game, two players, Maker and Breaker, alternately claim unclaimed edges of $G$, and Maker wins if in the end of the game the graph spanned by Maker's edges contains a copy of $H$. Otherwise, Breaker wins the game. We call a graph $G$ winnable for $H$ if Maker has a winning strategy for the Maker-Breaker $H$-game on $G$, and we call it minimal winnable if additionally Breaker wins the $H$-game on every proper subgraph of $G$. Along the lines of minimal-Ramsey theory, we characterize all graphs $H$ for which there exist infinitely many minimal winnable graphs, and we prove tight bounds for the smallest minimum degree among all these minimal winnable graphs. Amongst others, we obtain precise results for trees, cycles, cliques, and complete bipartite graphs. In general, we find many similarities between the Ramsey setting and the Maker-Breaker setting, but we also show substantial differences.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Allin, Juri Barkey, Dennis Clemens

item.title: Descartes' rule of signs for polynomial systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.06435v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical Descartes' rule of signs bounds the number of positive roots of a real polynomial in one variable by the number of sign changes of its coefficients. This bound only depends on the order of the exponents and on the signs of the coefficients, that is, on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices. We generalize this rule to fewnomial systems with any number of monomials: for systems of $n$ real polynomial equations in $n$ variables with $n+k+1$ monomials, we obtain upper bounds for the number of nondegenerate positive solutions which only depend on sign conditions on the maximal minors of the coefficient matrix and of the exponent matrix and its liftings. For $k=1$ they are the Descartes' rules of signs for circuits of Bihan--Dickenstein and Bihan--Dickenstein--Forsg{\aa}rd. Our approach starts from the Gale duality and the Khovanskii--Rolle argument of Bihan and Sottile, which reduce the problem to counting common zeros of iterated Jacobians in a chamber $\Delta$ of a hyperplane arrangement determined by the coefficients. We bound this number by the B\'ezout number minus the zeros forced in the other chambers by a topological degree, which we compute by a facet-count formula involving signs of minors of a Gale dual matrix of the exponent matrix. This leads to a recursion over the flats of the arrangement, which ends with the Descartes' rules for circuits. Restricting the recursion to coherent chambers, in which no cancellation occurs in the facet-count formula, gives weaker bounds in closed form.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Bihan

item.title: Topological degree of sparse polynomial maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.29808v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider maps $F\colon\R^n_{>0}\to\R^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support $\A$, and we study the topological degree of $F$. We prove a real analogue of the Bernstein--Kushnirenko--Khovanskii theorem, which says that the number of solutions in the complex torus is the normalized volume of the Newton polytope when there is no solution at infinity. Our main assumption is a half-space condition on the columns of the coefficient matrix indexed by the faces of the Newton polytope. It is a positive analogue of the absence of solutions at infinity, and it is satisfied for generic exponents and coefficients. Under this condition, we show that the topological degree only depends on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices restricted to the vertices of the Newton polytope. We give two closed formulas for it: a sum over the facets of the Newton polytope, and a Viro formula, which is a signed count of the positively decorated simplices of a regular triangulation of $\A$. As a consequence, we get sign conditions for the existence of positive solutions, as well as parity results for their number.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Bihan

item.title: Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers of $3$-graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32644v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A $3$-graph (meaning a $3$-uniform hypergraph) $H$ is iteratively $3$-partite if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of some lexicographic power of a single hyperedge. We prove a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstra\"{e}te, and Yu, that for a $3$-graph $H$, the off-diagonal Ramsey number $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$ if and only if $H$ is iteratively $3$-partite. As an immediate corollary, we also obtain a resolution of a 2009 problem of Bohman, Frieze and Mubayi, asking for a characterization of all $3$-graphs $H$ for which the minimum number of hyperedges in an $H$-free $3$-graph with chromatic number greater than $k$ is $k^{3+o(1)}$ as $k\to\infty$. We prove a $3$-graph $H$ has the latter property if and only if $H$ is not iteratively $3$-partite.
item.dc:creator: Lior Gishboliner, Sepehr Hajebi, Xiangyu Li

item.title: Cycles and Symmetries of Non-Transitive Dice with Minimal and Uniform Winning Advantages
item.description: arXiv:2610.40321v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider non-transitivity among dice with \(n\) sides restricted to taking face values in the set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). We investigate properties of the directed graphs arising from minimal and uniform winning advantages, including embeddings, isolated vertices and an involutive antiautomorphism. For every \(n\geq9\), we construct a non-transitive triple admitting no pairwise ties with uniform and minimal winning advantage. Moreover, for every \(n\geq7\), we construct a non-transitive triple which is invariant under the involutive antiautomorphism. We consider a two-player game utilizing these constructions and investigate the winning probabilities as \(n\) increases. We give a computer-assisted proof that \(n=6\) is the smallest \(n\geq3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage, and identify the two unique such cycles. Finally, we present computational evidence supporting a conjecture that \(n=6\) is also the largest such \(n\).
item.dc:creator: Terry Easlick

item.title: A linear edge bound for k-quasi-planar graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.01509v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the $k$-quasi-planar graph conjecture for topological drawings. For every integer $k\ge 2$, a simple graph on $n\ge 3$ vertices admitting a drawing with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges has at most $1056(k-1)^2(n-2)$ edges. Thus the number of edges is linear in $n$, with an explicit quadratic dependence on $k$. The result allows multiple crossings between the same pair of edges, including edges with a common endpoint. The proof uses the double of a sphere with boundary to represent graph edges by closed geodesics on a hyperbolic surface. The endpoints of geodesic lifts induce partial orders of width at most $k-1$. A stability bound for greedy chain partitions, together with a counting argument over a triangulation, gives the stated edge bound.
item.dc:creator: Ankan Sadhu

item.title: The proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: a detailed exposition and an extension to rotation systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.03515v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number $\ucr{K_n}$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is $Z(n):=\frac{1}{4}\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\rfloor$ for all $n\ge 3$. In October 2026 OpenAI uploaded to GitHub a proof of this conjecture. The proof is very short, but it relies on polynomial methods that are not part of the standard techniques used by many combinatorialists, and it is written with very little motivation or explanation. Since we found the proof very hard to follow, we decided to write this paper, which contains a complete proof of the conjecture written for mathematicians who are more familiar with combinatorics than with polynomial methods. In fact we prove a more general result on rotation systems of $K_n$, from which the Harary--Hill conjecture easily follows. Namely, we show that for every rotation system $\Pi$ of $K_n$ the number of $4$-vertex subsystems of $\Pi$ realizable as drawings of $K_4$ with one crossing, plus three times the number of non-realizable $4$-vertex subsystems of $\Pi$, is at least $Z(n)$. The statement and proof of our result are purely combinatorial and do not involve drawings at all.
item.dc:creator: Gelasio Salazar

item.title: Polyhedral Geometry of Degree-Bounded Characteristic Imset Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.09633v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Characteristic imset polytopes are convex hulls of a collection of characteristic imset vectors, which are 0/1 vectors that encode the Markov equivalence class of a directed acyclic graph. These polytopes are the feasible region of linear programs which correspond to causal discovery problems. We introduce a new family of these polytopes whose vertices correspond to directed acyclic graphs with in-degree bounded by $k$. This yields a polytope whose dimension is only polynomial in the number of nodes of the underlying graphs instead of exponential. We show that when $k = 1$, this polytope is a matroid independence polytope. For $k = 2$ we provide several large families of facet-defining inequalities, which give a complete $\mathcal{H}$-representation of the polytope on four nodes.
item.dc:creator: Jane Ivy Coons, Benjamin Hollering, Niharika Chakrabarty Paul

item.title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.10985v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a graph $\Gamma$ with vertex set $V(\Gamma)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $\Gamma$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $\Gamma\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the \emph{connected zero forcing number} $Z_C(\Gamma)$. A \emph{connected zero forcing polynomial} of a finite graph $\Gamma$ is a monic polynomial $Z_C^{\Gamma}(x) \;=\; \sum_{k} a_k x^k$, where $a_k$ counts the number of connected zero forcing sets of $\Gamma$ of size $k$, which we denote by $Z_C(\Gamma,k)$. In this paper, we find the connected zero forcing polynomial of any finite tree $T$, and show that they are log-concave. We then establish sharp lower bounds for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices. We also identify a family of trees, which we call uniform trees, and we prove that for any tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, there exists a uniform tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, whose connected zero forcing polynomial bounds as an upper bound, the connected zero forcing polynomial of the tree coefficient wise. Again for $2\leq p\leq 4$, we establish a sharp upper bound for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices.
item.dc:creator: Sanjay Mukherjee, Papi Ray

item.title: Stabilization of zero forcing numbers of finite quotients of periodic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.13244v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a method for determining the zero forcing number of a graph by passing to an infinite cover. When the quotient map is a covering map, forcing commutes with taking preimages. If, in addition, the closure of every small set in the cover touches none of its translates, then no small set is a zero forcing set of the quotient. For covers that are periodic, this condition reduces to a property of the cover alone, and it gives an explicit threshold beyond which the zero forcing number of the quotient equals that of the cover. We apply the method to the generalized Petersen graphs: $Z(P(n,k))=2k+2$ for all $k\ge 1$ and $n\ge 2k^2+k+1$. We also show that the circulant $C_n(1,a)$ has zero forcing number $2a$ for all $n\ge 2a^2-a+1$.
item.dc:creator: Young H. Kim, Youngsoo Kim, Byunghoon Lee

item.title: Golomb rulers with real marks: the real and integer optima agree up to ten marks
item.description: arXiv:2611.22656v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A Golomb ruler is a set of integer marks whose pairwise differences are distinct. We let the marks be real numbers and ask that every difference be at least 1 and that any two differences be at least 1 apart. Every integer Golomb ruler satisfies these conditions, so the least length $G_R(n)$ of such a real ruler with $n$ marks is at most the optimal Golomb length $G_Z(n)$. Fixing the order of all differences splits the real problem into finitely many polyhedral chambers. A branch-and-bound over these chambers, with an exact rational certificate at every leaf, proves $G_R(n) = G_Z(n)$ for $n \le 10$. Each proof takes under a minute and is verified by an independent checker that uses only exact arithmetic. An exhaustive exact enumeration of all chamber vertices confirms the result for $n \le 7$, and shows that there the shortest real rulers are exactly the optimal integer rulers and their mirror images. For every $n$ we have $n(\sqrt{n}-1)^2 \le G_R(n) \le G_Z(n)$, essentially a bound of Erd\H{o}s and of Cilleruelo and Ruzsa, so that $G_R(n) \sim G_Z(n) \sim n^2$. Non-integral chamber vertices first appear at $n = 7$: there are 84, all half-integral. Already there, 80 of them are shortest points of their chambers, 40 of them the only one, although the global optimum is integral; a twelve-mark example of the same kind comes from Singer's construction. On the other hand, every Singer ruler with at most 104 marks, cut at the largest gap, is the only shortest point of its own chamber; we conjectured this for all prime powers, and Ma and Zhang have since proved it.
item.dc:creator: Esther Notik

item.title: List packing for graphs with small arboricity
item.description: arXiv:2611.24832v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every graph $G$ whose edge set is the union of $r$ forests has list packing number at most $2^r$. This means that for all $k\ge 2^r$ and every list-assignment $L$ with lists of size $k$, the graph $G$ admits $k$ disjoint proper $L$-colourings. While for large $r$ this bound is far from optimal, for $r\in\{1,2\}$ it is sharp. As a direct corollary of the case $r=2$, we obtain that every triangle-free planar graph has list packing number at most $4$, thus improving upon a result of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Masa\v{r}\'ik, Mus\'ilek and Pangr\'ac and providing the optimal answer to a question of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Postle and Norin on (weighted) $\epsilon$-flexibility of such graphs. As a corollary of the case $r=3$, we obtain a short alternative proof that every $K_5$-minor-free (and hence every planar) graph has list-packing number at most $8$, matching the state of the art. All results above also hold for the stronger notion of correspondence packing.
item.dc:creator: Stijn Cambie, Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Xuding Zhu

item.title: Marked Persistent Homology: Circuits and Bordisms
item.description: arXiv:2209.01099v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The barcode of a persistence module does not determine the relations among prescribed cycles. We encode these relations by a filtration of kernels in fixed coordinates, whose circuits can ramify into overlapping families and later recombine, unlike the merge-tree structure of degree-zero persistence. The kernels recover the marked image module and admit simultaneous rational bordism realizations. An explicit planar Vietoris-Rips filtration exhibits the circuit changes and their surface fillings.
item.dc:creator: \.Ismail G\"uzel, Atabey Kaygun

item.title: P{\l}onka bi-magmas and the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation
item.description: arXiv:2305.14138v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a new variety of universal algebras with two binary operations, called \emph{P{\l}onka bi-magmas}, and use them to construct novel solutions to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter (YB) equation. We establish explicit structural and classification results for P{\l}onka bi-magmas, which allow for a detailed study of the induced families of YB-solutions. In particular, we identify and classify several naturally arising classes of YB-solutions from the universal algebra perspective, including the so-called bi-connected and ideal-simple ones. For instance, we prove that there are only countably many isomorphism classes of induced YB-solutions which are ideal-simple, and characterize them in terms of the odometer transformations familiar from ergodic theory. In particular, if $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, then the number of isomorphism classes of all the induced ideal-simple YB-solutions on $X$ is equal to the sum of all divisors of $n$.
item.dc:creator: A. L. Agore, A. Chirvasitu, G. Militaru

item.title: Likelihood Geometry of Reflexive Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2311.13572v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the problem of maximum likelihood (ML) estimation for statistical models defined by reflexive polytopes. Our focus is on the maximum likelihood degree of these models as an algebraic measure of complexity of the corresponding optimization problem. We compute the ML degrees of all 4319 classes of three-dimensional reflexive polytopes, and observe some surprising behavior in terms of the presence of gaps between ML degrees and degrees of the associated toric varieties. We interpret these drops in the context of discriminants and prove formulas for the ML degree for families of reflexive polytopes, including the hypercube and its dual, the cross polytope, in arbitrary dimension. In particular, we determine a family of embeddings for the $d$-cube that implies ML degree one. Finally, we discuss generalized constructions of families of reflexive polytopes in terms of their ML degrees.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Am\'endola, Janike Oldekop

item.title: A new class of affine $K(\pi,1)$ arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2512.00318v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that a certain class of affine hyperplane arrangements are $K(\pi,1)$ by endowing their Falk complexes with an injective metric. This gives new examples of infinite $K(\pi,1)$ arrangements in dimension $n>2$.
item.dc:creator: Katherine Goldman, Jingyin Huang

item.title: Product sets in sets of returns and positivity of symmetric ergodic averages
item.description: arXiv:2608.02873v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study sets of (measurable) returns in countable groups $G$, namely sets of the form $\{g\in G:\mu(A\cap T_gA)>0\}$ arising from measure-preserving actions. Extending a result of Bergelson, we show that sets of returns in $G\times G$ contain subsets of the form $B\times B$, where $B$ is large with respect to suitable notions of largeness that remain meaningful even for non-amenable groups. As a consequence, if $G$ is amenable, then every sufficiently large subset $A\subseteq G\times G$ satisfies $B\times B\subseteq AA^{-1}$ for some large set $B\subseteq G$. We also investigate when sets of returns in $G$ contain product sets $BB$ with $B$ large. In contrast with the Cartesian-product phenomenon above, this problem is considerably subtler in non-abelian groups and is closely connected to `symmetric correlation functions', namely functions of the form $g\mapsto \mu(T_g^{-1}A\cap T_gA)$. We use this connection to show that, for broad classes of amenable groups - including finitely generated nilpotent groups and certain solvable non-nilpotent groups, every sufficiently large set $A\subseteq G$ contains a large subset $B$ satisfying $BB\subseteq AA^{-1}$. Finally, we establish polynomial analogues of these results for finitely generated nilpotent groups, extending earlier work of Bergelson and Ruzsa.
item.dc:creator: Vitaly Bergelson, Sa\'ul Rodr\'iguez-Mart\'in

item.title: Origametry and antagonistic heptagon graphs: the braced {35,1} and the complete {21,2}
item.description: arXiv:2608.13592v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study two planar unit-distance graphs (UDGs) that both look like heptagons but have opposite rigidity yet kindred arithmetic: the braced heptagon {35,1} (19 vertices, 35 edges) and the complete heptagon {21,2} (21 vertices, 42 edges). Neither is straightedge-and-compass constructible -- already the regular 7-gon is not, by Gauss-Wantzel -- so the natural setting is origametry: the construction of each realization by Huzita-Hatori folds, with the quadratic fold O5 (straightedge-and-compass strength) versus the cubic Beloch fold O6. The complete heptagon is over-braced and globally rigid, with a unique realization whose 42 edges are certified unit exactly, with coordinates in Q(cos pi/42), of degree 12 (minimal over all placements), containing the cubic Q(cos 2pi/7): every vertex is an origami number. It is Haugland's H21, whose two heptagram layers are the seed of the 449-vertex 5-chromatic graph of Heule and Przybocki. The braced heptagon is isostatic (minimally rigid) with thousands of non-congruent realizations and a large generic realization count N = 3869504 = 2^6 * 103 * 587; yet we prove that its unit realization is again origami-constructible. In Pegg's explicit construction the pinning angle is a root of an irreducible degree-12 palindromic polynomial whose Chebyshev reduction, an irreducible sextic, factors into quadratics over the heptagon cubic Q(cos 2pi/7); hence the coordinate field is a {2,3}-tower of degree 3*2^k, reached by one trisection followed by quadratics. The primes 103 and 587 belong to the generic complex count, not to the folded coordinates. We solve the governing cubic by folding (Lill's method and the Beloch fold), place both graphs inside Alperin's field of origami numbers, and read the fold-branch signs of the construction as mountain-valley assignments with an empirical Maekawa-type balance. All claims are checked in exact arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Haroldo Costa Silva Filho, Edward Pegg Jr

item.title: Partial $F$-invariants and cluster categorifications
item.description: arXiv:2609.08781v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $F$-invariant in cluster algebras is a combinatorial invariant that unifies the $E$-invariant from additive categorification and the $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant from monoidal categorification. In this paper, we study its refinement, the partial $F$-invariant, and establish its mutation formula under changes of the initial seed. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Reading, which asserts that the non-compatible cluster variables can be separated by sign-coherence of $g$-vectors upon varying the initial seed. We further show that, for cluster monomials, the partial $F$-invariants coincide with both the partial $E$-invariants for reachable decorated representations of quivers with potentials and the pole orders of normalized $R$-matrices (or partial $\mathfrak{d}$-invariants) for finite-dimensional reachable simple modules over quantum affine algebras. As consequences, we obtain a combinatorial formula for the pole orders for reachable simple modules in terms of $q$-characters; we verify the conjectural explicit formula for the pole orders between Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules.
item.dc:creator: Peigen Cao, Ryo Fujita, Kota Murakami

item.title: Uniform Sampling of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.03578v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give exactly uniform samplers for linear codes with prescribed hull dimension, for the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic inner products and over finite fields of every characteristic. Except for the Euclidean form over fields of odd characteristic, these are the first uniform samplers for arbitrary prescribed hull dimension. Each sample costs an expected $O(k^2 N + k \log q)$ field operations for codes of dimension $k$ in a space of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ or $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.
item.dc:creator: Keita Ishizuka

item.title: Littlestone Dimension and Its Dual
item.description: arXiv:2611.26721v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The dual Littlestone dimension of a concept class $\mathcal{H}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$, $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}):=\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H}^*)$, is the Littlestone dimension of the dual class $\mathcal{H}^*$, obtained by exchanging the roles of domain points and hypotheses. A classical result of Shelah implies that $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})$ and $\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H})$ are finite simultaneously, and quantitative results of Hodges [Mathematika, 1981] imply the doubly exponential bound $\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}}$. Malliaris and Moran [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2024] asked whether this bound is optimal. We answer this by proving the bound \[ \operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal{H})\le 2^{O(\operatorname{Ldim}^*(\mathcal{H}))}, \] which is tight up to the constant in the exponent, as witnessed by the class of all binary hypotheses on a finite domain.
item.dc:creator: Pooya Hatami, Chavdar Lalov

item.title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
item.description: arXiv:2611.27300v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code of distance exactly $2$, so the girth is not a lower bound. For a represented Lagrangian matroid and a dealer, we construct the dealer-shortened stabilizer code, its logical operators, an encoding isometry and explicit recovery maps, and we show that this is the code implemented by the stabilizer state through teleportation. A set of players recovers the secret, learns nothing, or learns part of it according to a rank formula on pairs of columns, which equals its mutual information with the dealer; for graph states it becomes a cut-rank condition. Over $\F_2$ a symplectic matroid of any rank has only one representation, so the code, its access structure and its weight enumerators depend on the matroid alone; for $q\ge3$ even the enumerator does not. Circuit-induced authorized sets always reconstruct when the matroid is self-dual, but not in general, and a six-qubit graph state shows that the two access structures can differ even then. Finally, a polynomial in the ranks of column pairs determines both weight enumerators.
item.dc:creator: Sayantan Ganguly
